nahhas-irab:24-24.t:
﴿قُلْ مَنْ يَرْزُقُكُمْ مِنَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ قُلِ اللَّهُ وَإِنَّا أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لَعَلى هُدىً أَوْ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ (24)

(قُلْ مَنْ يَرْزُقُكُمْ مِنَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ قُلِ اللَّهُ): (مَنْ) is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is a complete noun because it is interrogative; (يَرْزُقُكُمْ) is in the position of the khabar (predicate). It is permissible to assimilate the qāf into the kāf, so that the qāf is changed into a kāf. (وَإِنَّا): the original is «وإنّنا», and the nūn was dropped for lightness. (أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the noun of «إنّ»; had it been conjoined to the position, it would have been «أو أنتم». (لَعَلى هُدىً) would then belong to the first only, if you said «أو أنتم»; but when you say «أو إيّاكم», it is more fitting that it belong to the second, and it has been omitted from the first. It may also belong to the first, and this is the choice of Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad]. He said: its meaning is the meaning of the words of one who seeks help against his companion regarding the truth of the threat, relying on the clear proof: "One of us is a liar," when the meaning is already known; and as you say: "I do such-and-such and you do such-and-such, and one of us is mistaken," when it is already known that he is the one mistaken. So it is with (وَإِنَّا أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لَعَلى هُدىً أَوْ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ).

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: (قُلْ أَرُونِيَ الَّذِينَ أَلْحَقْتُمْ بِهِ شُرَكاءَ): (أَرُونِيَ) here is from seeing with the heart (i.e. knowing), meaning: make known to me these idols and images which you have made partners to Allah, Mighty and Majestic — have they shared with Him in the creation of anything? Then make clear what it is; otherwise, why do you worship them? It may also be from seeing with the eye, in which case «شركاء» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the meaning is "Show me those whom you have joined to Him as partners"; then [the pronoun] was omitted because it is in the ṣila (relative clause). He said: then He, Mighty and Majestic, said (كَلَّا): a deterrent and a warning, i.e. desist from this statement and become aware of your error.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: (وَما أَرْسَلْناكَ إِلَّا كَافَّةً): accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "We have sent you gathering people together," because he ﷺ was sent to the Arabs and the non-Arabs.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: The grammarians permitted «لكم ميعادٌ يومٌ» [with يوم in the nominative] as a badal (substitute) for «ميعاد», and they permitted «ميعادٌ يوماً لا تستأخرون عنه» with it as an adverb (ẓarf), the hāʾ [in «عنه»] then referring back to «يوم»; and the genitive construct is then not permissible, just as you say: «إنّ يوماً زيدٌ فيه أميرٌ عبدُ الله فيه وزيرٌ» ("On a day on which Zayd is governor, ʿAbd Allāh is minister in it"), with tanwīn on «يوم» and nothing else. If you omit «فيه», it is permissible [Translator's note: the text reads «جار», evidently for «جاز» "it is permissible"] to drop the tanwīn and to put «عبد الله» in the accusative as the noun of «إنّ». It is also permissible: (مِيعادُ يَوْمٍ لا تَسْتَأْخِرُونَ) without tanwīn on «يوم», on the basis that the hāʾ in «عنه» refers back to «ميعاد», not to «يوم».

nahhas-irab:31-31.t:
Saʿīd reported from Qatāda: (وَلا بِالَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ) — of the Books and the Prophets, peace be upon them.
(وَلَوْ تَرى إِذِ الظَّالِمُونَ مَوْقُوفُونَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ): (الظَّالِمُونَ) are nominative by being the mubtadaʾ (subject), and (مَوْقُوفُونَ) is its khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa (genitive construct). It is not permissible to put «موقوفون» in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because «إذ» is an adverb of time and so cannot be a predicate about concrete bodies. The apodosis (jawāb) of «لو» is omitted because the hearer knows it. (يَرْجِعُ بَعْضُهُمْ إِلى بَعْضٍ الْقَوْلَ), i.e. answers him; and this is the eloquent usage: one says «رجعتُ زيداً» ("I answered Zayd"). (يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا لَوْلا أَنْتُمْ لَكُنَّا مُؤْمِنِينَ): this is the eloquent usage. Among the Arabs are some who say «لولاكم»; Sībawayh reported it, and «لولا» then puts the pronoun in the genitive, while it raises the overt noun after it to the nominative as mubtadaʾ and its khabar is omitted. Muḥammad ibn Zayd says «لولاكم» is not permissible, because the pronoun follows the overt noun, and since the overt noun is nominative by consensus, the pronoun must likewise be nominative. [Translator's note: "Muḥammad ibn Zayd" is as written; elsewhere the author cites Muḥammad ibn Yazīd (al-Mubarrad), who is known for rejecting «لولاك».]

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: (بَلْ كُنْتُمْ مُجْرِمِينَ): i.e. you chose disbelief, and we had no way over you except that we called you and you responded to us.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t:
(بَلْ مَكْرُ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ): al-Akhfash said: i.e. this is the plotting of the night and the day. Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning — and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows best — is "your plotting in the night and the day", i.e. your counselling us and your calling us to the disbelief which brought us to this. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: i.e. "rather, your plotting night and day", as the Arabs say «نهاره صائم، وليله قائم» ("his day is fasting and his night is standing in prayer"), and he recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 346-
لقد لمتنا يا أمّ غيلان في السّرى ... ونمت وما ليل المطيّ بنائم
(You blamed us, O Umm Ghaylān, for travelling by night — and you slept, while the night of the riding-camels is not asleep.)
And Sībawayh recited: [al-Rajaz] 347-
فنام ليلي وتجلّى همّي
(So my night slept and my care was lifted.)
i.e. I slept in it. Jaʿfar ibn Abī al-Mughīra reported from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: (بَلْ مَكْرُ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ) — he said: the passing of the night and the day over them, so they became heedless. Rāshid read (بَلْ مَكْرُ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ) in the accusative, as one says «رأيته مقدمَ الحاجّ» ("I saw him at the time of the pilgrims' arrival"); this is only permissible with what is well known — had you said «رأيته مقدمَ زيد», it would not be permissible. (إِذْ تَأْمُرُونَنا أَنْ نَكْفُرَ بِاللَّهِ وَنَجْعَلَ لَهُ أَنْداداً): he said: one also says «نديد» [for «ندّ», an equal], and he recited: [al-Wāfir] 348-
أتيما تجعلون إليّ ندّا ... وما تيم لذي حسب نديد
(Do you make Taym an equal to me? Taym is no equal to a man of noble lineage.)
(وَأَسَرُّوا النَّدامَةَ لَمَّا رَأَوُا الْعَذابَ): there are two views on its meaning. One of them is that the meaning of «أسرّوا» is "they showed openly", and that it is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād), as he said: [al-Ṭawīl] 349-
تجاوزت أحراسا إليها ومعشرا ... عليّ حراصا لو يسرّون مقتلي
(I passed by guards to reach her, and a clan eager against me, who would gladly make known [or: conceal] my killing.)
It has also been transmitted as «يشرّون». And it was said: «وأسرّوا الندامة» means the remorse became evident in the lines (asrār) of their faces. And it was said: remorse does not appear; it is only in the heart, and what appears is only what arises from it.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: (إِلَّا قالَ مُتْرَفُوها): Saʿīd reported from Qatāda: (مُتْرَفُوها) means its tyrants, its chiefs and the leaders of evil.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: The best of what has been said about this is what al-Ḥasan said: he said, "He chooses for him [what is best]." The meaning, according to his view, of (وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it as a trial, and does for them what is best for them.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
﴿وَما أَمْوالُكُمْ وَلا أَوْلادُكُمْ بِالَّتِي تُقَرِّبُكُمْ عِنْدَنا زُلْفى إِلاَّ مَنْ آمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صالِحاً فَأُولئِكَ لَهُمْ جَزاءُ الضِّعْفِ بِما عَمِلُوا وَهُمْ فِي الْغُرُفاتِ آمِنُونَ﴾ (37)

(وَما أَمْوالُكُمْ وَلا أَوْلادُكُمْ بِالَّتِي تُقَرِّبُكُمْ عِنْدَنا زُلْفى): al-Akhfash said: i.e. «أزلافاً» (a drawing near); it is a noun of the maṣdar (verbal noun). Al-Farrāʾ claimed that «التي» is for the wealth and the children together. He has another view, which is the position of Abū Isḥāq: the meaning would be "Your wealth is not that which brings you near to Us in nearness, nor are your children that which brings you near to Us in nearness," and then [one of them] was omitted. Al-Farrāʾ recited: [al-Khafīf] 350-
نحن بما عندنا وأنت بما عندك ... راض والرّأي مختلف
(We with what we have, and you with what you have, are content — and opinion differs.)
And he recited: [al-Kāmil] 351-
إنّي ضمنت بما أتاني ما جنى ... وأبي وكان وكنت غير غدور
(I have guaranteed what came to me of what he committed — and my father too; he was, and I was, not treacherous.)
Outside the Qurʾān, «باللتين», «باللاتي», «باللواتي» and «بالذين» — the last for the children specifically — would be permissible. (إِلَّا مَنْ آمَنَ) is in the position of the accusative by exception. Abū Isḥāq claimed that it is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) for the kāf and mīm in «تقربكم»; this view seems to be an error, because the kāf and mīm are for the one addressed, so a badal is not permissible; were this permissible, «رأيتك زيداً» would be permissible. This view of Abū Isḥāq is the view of al-Farrāʾ, except that al-Farrāʾ does not say "badal", because that is not part of the terminology of the Kufans; but his view comes down to that. He claimed that similar to it is (إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ) [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 89], which in his view is accusative by «ينفع». Al-Farrāʾ also permitted «مَن» in His words, Mighty and Majestic, (بِالَّتِي تُقَرِّبُكُمْ عِنْدَنا زُلْفى إِلَّا مَنْ آمَنَ) to be in the position of the nominative, in the sense of "it is none but whoever believes" — so he said, and I cannot make out its meaning.
(فَأُولئِكَ لَهُمْ جَزاءُ الضِّعْفِ بِما عَمِلُوا): the grammarians permitted «أولئك لهم جزاءٌ الضعفُ», [الضعف] being a badal for «جزاء» or on the implication of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); they permitted «أولئك لهم جزاءٌ الضعفَ» in the sense of "those will have that We recompense them the double"; and they permitted «أولئك لهم جزاءً الضعفُ». [Translator's note: the source text gives these three variants without vowel marks, so they look identical; the case endings shown are supplied from the explanations given.] Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "those will have the double as recompense", i.e. in the state of their being recompensed. (وَهُمْ فِي الْغُرُفاتِ آمِنُونَ): from al-Ḥasan, «في الغُرْفات» with the rāʾ made quiescent; and from al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza, «في الغرفة». Abū Jaʿfar said: «الغرفات» is the plural of «غرفة» as a sound plural, except that the rāʾ was given ḍamma to distinguish between the noun and the adjective. Whoever says «غُرْفات» dropped the ḍamma because of its heaviness, and whoever says «غُرَفات» replaced the ḍamma with a fatḥa because it is lighter. «غُرُفات» may also be the plural of «غُرُف». Whoever read (الْغُرْفَةَ) brought a singular that indicates a group; the plural is more fitting, because the statement is about a group.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: (وَما أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَهُوَ يُخْلِفُهُ): this concerns what is spent in obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; it is replaced without doubt, either in this world or in the Hereafter. (وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ), i.e. [better than those who] provide for the servants.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: (وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعاً): [جميعاً] as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (ثُمَّ يَقُولُ لِلْمَلائِكَةِ أَهؤُلاءِ إِيَّاكُمْ كانُوا يَعْبُدُونَ): Saʿīd reported from Qatāda: this is a question like His words, Mighty and Majestic, to ʿĪsā, peace be upon him: (أَأَنْتَ قُلْتَ لِلنَّاسِ اتَّخِذُونِي وَأُمِّي إِلهَيْنِ) [al-Māʾida: 116]. Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning is that when the angels, Allah's blessings be upon them, give them the lie, that is a rebuke to them.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: (قالُوا سُبْحانَكَ أَنْتَ وَلِيُّنا مِنْ دُونِهِمْ), i.e. You are the One who takes charge of us, not they. (بَلْ كانُوا يَعْبُدُونَ الْجِنَّ), i.e. they obeyed them. (أَكْثَرُهُمْ بِهِمْ مُؤْمِنُونَ): by their accepting from them; and this is figurative (majāz).

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: (قُلْ إِنَّما أَعِظُكُمْ بِواحِدَةٍ): Sufyān reported from Layth from Mujāhid: «بواحدة» — he said: "There is no god but Allah." Others said: its implied form is "with one trait", and then He explained it by His words, Mighty and Majestic: (أَنْ تَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ مَثْنى وَفُرادى). «أن» is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) for «واحدة», or in the position of the nominative on the implication of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). The position of Abū Isḥāq is that it is in the position of the accusative, in the sense of «لأن تقوموا» ("in order that you stand"). (مَثْنى وَفُرادى) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it is a diptote for two reasons which we have mentioned. (ثُمَّ تَتَفَكَّرُوا) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «تقوموا».

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «علّامَ الغيوب» as a badal (substitute), i.e. «قل إنّ ربّي علّامَ الغيوب يقذف بالحقّ». Abū Isḥāq said: the nominative is from two angles: on the position, because the position is nominative; and as a badal for what is in «يقذف». Abū Jaʿfar said: there are two further ways for the nominative: it may be a khabar (predicate) after a khabar, and it may be on the implication of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the nominative in the like of this is more frequent in the speech of the Arabs when it comes after the khabar of «إنّ», and similar to it is (إِنَّ ذلِكَ لَحَقٌّ تَخاصُمُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ) [Ṣād: 64].

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: (قُلْ جاءَ الْحَقُّ): Saʿīd reported from Qatāda; he said: the Qurʾān. Abū Jaʿfar said: the implied form is "the possessor of the truth has come", i.e. the Book containing the true proofs and arguments. (وَما يُبْدِئُ الْباطِلُ): Saʿīd reported from Qatāda; he said: falsehood is Iblīs; and the implied form in Arabic is "the possessor of falsehood". Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: falsehood is the [false] gods; and he said: «وما يبدئ وما يعيد», i.e. it does not give life and does not cause death. Qatāda said: (ما يُبْدِئُ) «وما يعيد» — it does not create and does not resurrect. Others said: «ما يُبْدِئُ الْباطِلُ», i.e. it does not initiate an argument, and «ما يُعِيدُ», it does not relate an argument from someone else. The first «ما» is in the position of the accusative by «يبدئ», and the second «ما» in the position of the accusative by «يعيد». Abū Isḥāq said: it is better that «ما» be negative.

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: (قُلْ إِنْ ضَلَلْتُ فَإِنَّما أَضِلُّ عَلى نَفْسِي): a condition and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and likewise (وَإِنِ اهْتَدَيْتُ فَبِما يُوحِي إِلَيَّ رَبِّي). If you make «ما» mean «الذي» (that which), the hāʾ [referring pronoun] is omitted; and if you make it a maṣdar (verbal noun), it does not need a referring pronoun. (إِنَّهُ سَمِيعٌ قَرِيبٌ), i.e. He hears whoever calls on Him, and is near in answering him.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: (وَلَوْ تَرى إِذْ فَزِعُوا فَلا فَوْتَ): the apodosis (jawāb) of «لو» is omitted. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "Were you to see when they are terrified, you would see something from which a strong lesson is taken"; i.e. «فلا فوت لهم» — there is no escape for them, i.e. escape is not possible for them.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read (وَأَنَّى لَهُمُ التَّناوُشُ) with hamza [«التناؤش»]. Abū ʿUbayd considered this reading far-fetched, because «التناؤش» is remoteness, so it would be: "How could they have remoteness from a far place?" Abū Jaʿfar said: the reading is permissible and good, and it has two explanations in the speech of the Arabs, and one need not take it in this far-fetched way. One of the two explanations is that the original is without hamza, and then the wāw was given hamza because the vowel on it is weak; that is frequent in the speech of the Arabs. In the muṣḥaf transmitted by the many from the many is (وَإِذَا الرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ) [al-Mursalāt: 11], the original being «وُقِّتَتْ», because it is derived from «الوقت» (time). And one says, as the plural of «دار»: «أدؤر». The other explanation has been mentioned by Abū Isḥāq; he said: it is derived from «النئيش», which is movement with slowness, i.e. whence will they have movement towards what has become remote, when they disbelieved in it before?

nahhas-irab:53-53.t: (وَيَقْذِفُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ مِنْ مَكانٍ بَعِيدٍ): the Arabs say of everyone who speaks of what he has no right to [know]: "He hurls and casts at the unseen." (مِنْ مَكانٍ بَعِيدٍ) is a comparison to one who throws and does not hit with his throw. Whoever read «وَيُقْذَفُونَ» [passive], its meaning according to him is: it is hurled at them by those who lead them astray and misguide them. [Translator's note: the source prints this second reading with the same vowelling as the first, (وَيَقْذِفُونَ); the variant meant is evidently the passive «ويُقذَفون».]

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: (وَحِيلَ بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ ما يَشْتَهُونَ): it was said: a barrier was placed between them and escape from the punishment; and it was said: a barrier was placed between them and what they desired in this world of their wealth and families. The position of Qatāda is that the meaning is that they desired that it be accepted from them that they obey Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and stop at what He commands them, and a barrier was placed between them and that, because that was only [possible] in this world, and it had passed away at that time. The original of «حِيل» is «حُوِل»; the vowel of the wāw was transferred to the ḥāʾ, so it changed into a yāʾ, and its vowel was dropped because of its heaviness. [Translator's note: the source says «فقلبت حركة الواو على الحاء», literally "the vowel of the wāw was turned onto the ḥāʾ".] (إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا فِي شَكٍّ), i.e. in the world, and about Divine Unity; (مُرِيبٍ), i.e. causing suspicion.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: [Translator's note: the entry concerns ﴿الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي لَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾.] ﴿الَّذِي﴾ is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) or badal (substitute); it may be in the position of the nominative by an implied (muḍmar) mubtadaʾ (subject), and in the position of the accusative in the sense of "I mean" (aʿnī). Sībawayh related: الحمد لله أهل الحمد ("Praise be to Allah, the One worthy of praise") with the accusative, the nominative and the genitive. ﴿وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf).

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لا تَأْتِينَا السَّاعَةُ قُلْ بَلى وَرَبِّي﴾: an oath, and the answer is ﴿لَتَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ﴾. The people of Medina read عالمُ الغيب with the nominative, because the answer to the oath has already come first, so the nominative is good, as mubtadaʾ (subject) with what follows as its khabar (predicate); it may also be nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ, and the accusative is permissible in the sense of "I mean". Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim read ﴿عالِمِ الْغَيْبِ﴾ as a naʿt (adjective); and the rest of the Kufans read علّامِ الغيب, also in the genitive as a naʿt. عالم is for a little and a lot, and علّام is for a lot only; the usual and most fitting in the like of this is عالم الغيب, whereas if you say علّام الغيوب, علّام is more fitting. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Kisāʾī read لا يعزِب with kasra on the zāy; one says عزب يعزُب and يعزِب. Al-Farrāʾ said: the kasra is dearer to me, and it is the reading of al-Aʿmash. ﴿وَلا أَصْغَرُ مِنْ ذلِكَ وَلا أَكْبَرُ﴾: with fatḥa [i.e. أصغرَ, أكبرَ], conjoining them to «ذرّة»; and the reading of the generality is with the nominative, by conjunction to مثقال. [Translator's note: the Qur'anic quotation in the printed text bears the nominative vowelling, while the remark refers to the reading with fatḥa.]

nahhas-irab:4-5.t:
﴿لِيَجْزِيَ﴾: accusative [subjunctive] by the lām of purpose (lām kay); the implied meaning is "it will surely come to you, so that He may recompense".
Ṭalḥa and ʿĪsā read ﴿أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ مِنْ رِجْزٍ أَلِيمٌ﴾ with the nominative [أليمٌ], as a naʿt (adjective) of عذاب.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
﴿وَيَرَى﴾ is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to ليجزي; it may be in the position of the nominative as resumptive. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ is in the position of the nominative by يرى. ﴿أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ﴾: [العلم is] the khabar of [the verb] whose agent is not named (i.e. the passive) [Translator's note: so in the text; the object of the passive verb is evidently meant]. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ is in the position of the accusative as the first object of يرى. ﴿هُوَ الْحَقَّ﴾: [الحقّ is] the second object, and «هو» is a separating pronoun (fāṣila), which the Kufans call ʿimād ("support"). The nominative is also permissible, with «هو» as mubtadaʾ (subject) and «الحقّ» its khabar (predicate). According to all the grammarians the accusative is more frequent where there is the alif and lām, and likewise with an indefinite noun that does not take the alif and lām and so resembles a definite one. If the khabar is a known proper name, as in your saying كان أخوك هو زيد ("your brother was Zayd"), al-Farrāʾ claimed that the preferred choice in it is the nominative, and likewise كان أبو محمد هو عمرو.
His reason for preferring the nominative is that, since it has no alif and lām, it resembles the indefinite in the saying كان زيد هو جالس ("Zayd was, he is sitting"), because in this only the nominative is permissible.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هَلْ نَدُلُّكُمْ عَلى رَجُلٍ﴾: if you wish you may assimilate the lām into the nūn, because of its closeness to it. ﴿يُنَبِّئُكُمْ إِذا مُزِّقْتُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ﴾: the meaning is "he says to you". «إذا» is in the position of the accusative, and what governs it is مزّقتم. What governs it cannot be ينبئكم, because he is not informing them at that time; nor can what governs it be what follows إنّ, because that does not govern what precedes it. Abū Isḥāq permitted what governs it to be omitted, the implied meaning being: "when you have been utterly torn apart, you will be resurrected".

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿أَفْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً أَمْ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ بَلِ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ فِي الْعَذابِ وَالضَّلالِ الْبَعِيدِ﴾ (8) ﴿أَفْتَرى﴾: when the interrogative alif entered, the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) was dispensed with, so you dropped it; and the interrogative alif has fatḥa to distinguish it from the connecting alif.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا داوُدَ مِنَّا فَضْلًا﴾: two objects. ﴿يا جِبالُ أَوِّبِي مَعَهُ وَالطَّيْرَ﴾: i.e. echo back the plaintive chanting; the mountains would answer him when he recited the Psalms. It is from آب يؤوب, when one returns. والطيرُ with the nominative is the reading of al-Aʿraj and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. The nominative is from two angles: one is by conjunction to جبال, and the other by conjunction to the implied pronoun in أوّبي; that is good because after it comes «معه». The accusative, according to Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, is in the sense of "and We subjected the birds to him". Al-Kisāʾī said: it is conjoined to فضلا, i.e. "We gave him the birds". According to Sībawayh it is conjoined to the position, i.e. "We called the mountains and the birds". It may be a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), as you say استوى الماءُ والخشبةَ ("the water rose level with the post"), i.e. with the post. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū Isḥāq permit قمت وزيداً ("I stood up with Zayd"). ﴿وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ الْحَدِيدَ﴾: it is said:
he was the first for whom iron was made subservient; and it is said that he was given such strength that he could bend iron — and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best about that. Al-Ḥasan said: David ﷺ would take the iron and it would be in his hand like dough, and he would make coats of mail from it.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿أَنِ اعْمَلْ سابِغاتٍ﴾: Abū Isḥāq has two answers on it: one is that «أن» is in the sense of أي, explicative (mufassira), conveying the meaning "We said to him: Make"; the other answer is that it is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "and We softened iron for him for it [i.e. for making them]", and أن is joined to the imperative form. ﴿سابِغاتٍ﴾ is in the position of the accusative; the adjective stands in place of the thing described, i.e. "make ample coats of mail". دروع is feminine when it is [coats of mail] for war, while درع المرأة (a woman's chemise) is masculine. ﴿وَقَدِّرْ فِي السَّرْدِ﴾: Ibn ʿUyayna said from Ibn Abī Najīḥ from Mujāhid: [it is] the measure of the nail: it should not be thin so that it works loose, nor thick so that it splits it [the ring].

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
﴿وَلِسُلَيْمانَ الرِّيحَ﴾: al-Kisāʾī made it co-ordinated with ﴿وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ الْحَدِيدَ﴾ and said the meaning is:
"And We made the wind soft (gentle) for Solomon." Abū Isḥāq said: the implied meaning is "and We subjected the wind to Solomon". ʿĀṣim read ولسليمانَ الريحُ with the nominative [Translator's note: the printed quotation bears the accusative vowelling; the nominative is meant], as mubtadaʾ (subject), or by [the verb of] being settled (al-istiqrār), i.e. "to Solomon belongs the wind, established", and that same meaning is in it. If someone says: when you say أعطيت زيداً ديناراً ولعمرٍو درهمٌ ("I gave Zayd a dinar, and ʿAmr has a dirham"), using the nominative, it does not carry the meaning of the first, and it is possible that you did not give him the dirham — it is answered: the matter is so, [but] the verse is otherwise in meaning; it is known that no one subjected it except Allah, Majestic and Mighty. ﴿غُدُوُّها شَهْرٌ﴾: i.e. a month's journey; and likewise ﴿وَرَواحُها شَهْرٌ﴾. Al-Aʿmash related from al-Minhāl from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When Solomon ﷺ sat, four hundred thousand chairs would be set up around him; then the chiefs of mankind would sit next to him, the lowly of mankind next to them, the chiefs of the jinn next to the lowly of mankind, and the lowly of the jinn next to them. Over every chair was appointed a bird that attended to it; then the wind would carry them, and the birds would shade them from the sun. He would set out in the morning from Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) to Iṣṭakhr and take his midday rest there, then set out in the afternoon from Iṣṭakhr and spend the night in Jerusalem. Then Ibn ʿAbbās recited ﴿غُدُوُّها شَهْرٌ وَرَواحُها شَهْرٌ﴾. ﴿وَمِنَ الْجِنِّ مَنْ يَعْمَلُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾: «من» is in the position of the accusative in the sense of "and We subjected"; and it may be in the position of the nominative, as preceded regarding الريح. ﴿وَمَنْ يَزِغْ مِنْهُمْ عَنْ أَمْرِنا نُذِقْهُ مِنْ عَذابِ السَّعِيرِ﴾: a condition and its apodosis. ﴿مَنْ﴾ is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and it is complete.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t:
﴿يَعْمَلُونَ لَهُ ما يَشاءُ مِنْ مَحارِيبَ وَتَماثِيلَ﴾: the two are diptotes because this plural has no counterpart among singulars and is not pluralised as other plurals are pluralised. المحراب in the language is any elevated place; that towards which one prays is called a miḥrāb because it ought to be elevated and honoured. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «من محاريب», i.e. of mosques; and تماثيل, he said: images. Some said: making images is permissible because of this verse and because of what Allah, Majestic and Mighty, related about the Messiah ﷺ. Others said: the prohibition of them from the Prophet ﷺ is authentic, as is the threat against whoever makes them or takes them up; so he ﷺ abrogated what had been permitted before him. There was wisdom in that, because he ﷺ was sent when images were being worshipped, and it was most beneficial to remove them. ﴿وَجِفانٍ كَالْجَوابِ وَقُدُورٍ راسِياتٍ﴾: it is preferable that it be with yāʾ [i.e. كالجوابي]; whoever drops the yāʾ says: the way of the alif and lām is to enter an indefinite noun without changing it from its state; so since one says «جوابٍ», when the alif and lām entered it was left in its state with the yāʾ dropped. The singular of الجوابي is جابية, which is the great cauldron and the large basin into which a thing is collected (yujbā), i.e. gathered; from this is جبيت الخراج ("I collected the land-tax") and جبيت الجراد, i.e. I spread out a cloak and gathered them into it. However, Layth related from Mujāhid that he said:
الجوابي is the plural of جوبة. Abū Jaʿfar said: الجوبة is a large hollow in a mountain in which rainwater collects. ﴿وَقُدُورٍ راسِياتٍ﴾: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: they are copper cauldrons found in Persia. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: they are cauldrons that were made from the rocks of the mountains. ﴿اعْمَلُوا آلَ داوُدَ شُكْراً﴾: i.e. it is said to them.
﴿آلَ داوُدَ﴾: a vocative in a construct (nidāʾ muḍāf). According to Abū Isḥāq the accusative of شكرا is from two angles: one is "work for the sake of thanks", i.e. so that you may thank Allah, Majestic and Mighty; and the other is that the implied meaning is "give thanks with thanks" [i.e. a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)]. ﴿وَقَلِيلٌ مِنْ عِبادِيَ الشَّكُورُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). الشكور is for intensification only, while شاكر applies to little and much. Thanks (al-shukr) is only for a specific thing, and praise (al-ḥamd) is more general than it.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
﴿مِنْسَأَتَهُ﴾ is the reading of the people of Medina and Abū ʿAmr, and the Kufans read it with hamza. [Translator's note: so in the printed text; from what follows the reading of the Medinans and Abū ʿAmr is مِنْسَاتَه without hamza.] Its derivation indicates that it has a hamza, because it is derived from نسأته, i.e. I delayed it and pushed it; so it was called منسأة because a thing is pushed and delayed with it. Mujāhid and ʿIkrima said: it is the staff. Whoever read (منساته) replaced the hamza with alif. If someone says: substitution for the hamza is ugly and is permissible only in poetry, remotely and anomalously, and the like of this would not escape Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, especially as the people of Medina follow this reading — the answer to this is that the Arabs used substitution in this word and pronounced it thus, as substitution occurs elsewhere, and it is not made a basis for analogy; so much so that Abū ʿAmr said: "I do not know what it is from,
except that it has no hamza." And this is the speech of the learned, because what has a hamza may have its hamza left out, whereas what has no hamza may not be given a hamza in any way. ﴿فَلَمَّا خَرَّ تَبَيَّنَتِ الْجِنُّ﴾: his death. [Translator's note: something appears to be missing before the next sentence, as no first speaker is named.] Someone else said: the meaning is "the matter of the jinn became clear", like ﴿وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 82]. And it is said that the meaning is "the jinn became clear to mankind". In the exegesis with sound chains of transmission there is an explanation of the meaning: Ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Solomon son of David, Allah's blessings be upon them both, remained for a year without his death being known, leaning on his staff, while the jinn went about what he had commanded them; then he fell after a year. Ibn ʿAbbās read: فلما خرّ تبيّنت الإنس أن لو كان الجنّ يعلمون الغيب ما لبثوا في العذاب المهين ("When he fell, mankind realised that, had the jinn known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment"). Abū Jaʿfar said: this reading from Ibn ʿAbbās is by way of exegesis. As for ﴿أَنْ﴾, its position is the nominative as a badal (substitute) for الجنّ, i.e. "it became clear that, had the jinn known the unseen…"; this is a badal al-ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion). It may also be in the position of the accusative in the sense of the lām [i.e. "because"].

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
﴿لَقَدْ كانَ لِسَبَإٍ﴾: fully declined, with tanwīn, as the name of the tribe-group (ḥayy); originally it is the name of a man, as came by specification (tawqīf) from the Prophet ﷺ. Abū ʿAmr read لقد كان لسبأَ without full declension [Translator's note: the printed quotation shows the tanwīn form; the diptote is meant], making it the name of the tribe (qabīla); this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, who argued that it is the name of a tribe from the fact that after it comes ﴿فِي مَسْكَنِهِمْ﴾; if it were as it was [Translator's note: so in the text; perhaps "as he said" is meant], it would have been في مساكنها. ﴿آيَةٌ﴾ is the noun (ism) of kāna, i.e. a sign indicating the power of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and His favour upon His servants: that He made for the people of Sabaʾ two gardens, on the right and the left, and of what collected of rain between two mountains, at whose face was a dyke (musannāt). Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān al-Juʿfī said: al-musannāt is what the people of Egypt call al-jisr ("the dam"); they would open it when they wished, and when their garden had been watered they would close it. ﴿جَنَّتانِ﴾ is a badal (substitute) for الآية; it may be nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); آية may be made accusative as the khabar (predicate) of kāna; and جنتين may also be made accusative as the khabar, outside the Qur'an.
The implied meaning [of what follows] is: it was said to them: "Eat of the provision of your Lord and give thanks to Him." Al-Farrāʾ said: the statement is complete [here]. ﴿بَلْدَةٌ﴾: nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "this is a land"; ﴿وَرَبٌّ﴾ likewise by an implied mubtadaʾ; ﴿غَفُورٌ﴾ is its naʿt (adjective). As for في مساكنهم, it is the reading of al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Abū ʿAmr. Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī and Ḥamza read ﴿فِي مَسْكَنِهِمْ﴾ [Translator's note: i.e. مَسْكَنِهم with fatḥa on the kāf], and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and al-Kisāʾī read في مسكِنهم with kasra on the kāf. Abū Jaʿfar said: «مساكن» is clearer in this, because it unites the wording and the meaning. If you say مسكنهم, there are two analyses in it: one is that it is a singular conveying a plural, and the other is that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), which is neither dualised nor pluralised, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said ﴿خَتَمَ اللَّهُ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ وَعَلى سَمْعِهِمْ وَعَلى أَبْصارِهِمْ﴾ [al-Baqara: 7], where السمع came in the singular; and likewise ﴿فِي مَقْعَدِ صِدْقٍ﴾ [al-Qamar: 55]. Whoever says مسكِن with kasra on the kāf makes it like مسجد, and it is outside analogy; its like is found only by hearing (samāʿ).

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿فَأَعْرَضُوا فَأَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ سَيْلَ الْعَرِمِ﴾: ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl said: «العرم» is the dyke (al-musannāt). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: العرم is any barrier between two things, which is what is called al-sikr ("the weir"); it is the plural of عرمة. ﴿وَبَدَّلْناهُمْ بِجَنَّتَيْهِمْ جَنَّتَيْنِ ذَواتَيْ أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ﴾: Abū ʿAmr read ذواتَي أُكُلِ خمطٍ without tanwīn, in a construct. [Translator's note: the printed quotation of Abū ʿAmr's reading shows the tanwīn; the construct form is meant.] The exegetes and al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, said: «الخمط» is the arāk tree. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: الخمط is anything that has changed to what is not desirable; milk is khamṭ when it turns sour. The better reading in his view is ﴿ذَواتَيْ أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ﴾ with tanwīn, as a naʿt (adjective) of أكل or a badal (substitute) for it, because in his view the produce is the khamṭ itself. As for the construct, the way to its permissibility is that its implied meaning be "possessing produce of sourness" or "produce of bitterness". ﴿وَشَيْءٍ مِنْ سِدْرٍ قَلِيلٍ﴾: al-Farrāʾ said: it is the samur (acacia).

nahhas-irab:17-17.t:
﴿ذلِكَ جَزَيْناهُمْ بِما كَفَرُوا﴾: Abū Isḥāq said: «ذلك» is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "We recompensed them with that". وهل يُجازى إلا الكفورُ ("And is any recompensed except the ungrateful?") is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim; and the Kufans except ʿĀṣim read ﴿وَهَلْ نُجازِي إِلَّا الْكَفُورَ﴾ ("And do We recompense any except the ungrateful?"). This is preferable according to Abū ʿUbayd, because before it is «جزيناهم», and He did not say جوزوا ("they were recompensed"). [Translator's note: the attribution of the two readings appears reversed in the printed text; in the standard transmission it is Ḥafṣ ʿan ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī who read نُجازي.] Abū Jaʿfar said: there is latitude in this matter, and the meaning in it is clear: if one person said "Allah, Majestic and Mighty, created Adam from clay" and another said "Adam was created from clay", the meaning would be the same. In the verse there is a question; I know of none in the sūra harder than it. It is asked: what is the meaning of "And is any recompensed except the ungrateful?", when He did not mention the people of sins other than the disbelievers? The scholars have discussed this. Some said:
no one is recompensed with the like of this recompense, which is extirpation and destruction, except whoever disbelieves. As for Quṭrub, his answer on this verse is otherwise, because he applied it to the people of sins other than the disbelievers, following his school, and his saying [was]: "whoever is ungrateful for the blessings and commits major sins". The best of what has been said about this verse, and the most eminent of what has been related about it, is that al-Ḥasan said: "like for like". Ayyūb related from Abū Mulayka [Translator's note: so in the text; Ibn Abī Mulayka is the known narrator] from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Whoever is brought to account is ruined." I said: "O Prophet of Allah, then what of His saying, Majestic and Mighty, ﴿فَسَوْفَ يُحاسَبُ حِساباً يَسِيراً﴾ [al-Inshiqāq: 8]?" He said: "That is only the presentation; and whoever is scrutinised in the reckoning is ruined." Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a sound chain. Its explanation is that the disbeliever is requited for his deeds and brought to account for them, and whatever good he did is nullified. What makes this clear to you is His saying, Majestic and Mighty, in the first ﴿ذلِكَ جَزَيْناهُمْ بِما كَفَرُوا﴾ and in the second «وهل يجازى»: the meaning of «يجازى» is "he is requited for what he did", and the meaning of «جزيناهم» is "We paid them in full". This is the literal sense of the language, even though جازى occurs in the sense of جزى figuratively.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t:
﴿وَجَعَلْنا بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ الْقُرَى الَّتِي بارَكْنا فِيها قُرىً ظاهِرَةً﴾: Abū al-ʿAbbās said: الظاهرة is the elevated. ﴿وَقَدَّرْنا فِيهَا السَّيْرَ﴾: i.e. We made it by measure, so that they travel and spend the night in a village. Al-Farrāʾ said: ﴿وَقَدَّرْنا فِيهَا السَّيْرَ﴾, i.e. We made [the distance] between every two villages half a day; this is the measuring.
﴿سِيرُوا فِيها لَيالِيَ وَأَيَّاماً﴾: two adverbs (ẓarf). ﴿آمِنِينَ﴾: as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
﴿فَقالُوا رَبَّنا باعِدْ بَيْنَ أَسْفارِنا﴾: there are six variant readings in it. [Translator's note: the vowelling that distinguishes the readings has largely been lost in the printed text; the intended forms, reconstructed from the author's explanations, are given in square brackets.] Al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, Abū Mālik, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read ﴿رَبَّنا باعِدْ بَيْنَ أَسْفارِنا﴾. Mujāhid, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read ربّنا بعد بين أسفارنا [رَبَّنا بَعِّدْ]. Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya read, and it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Ṣāliḥ, ربّنا باعد بين أسفارنا [رَبُّنا باعَدَ]. Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read, and it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, ربّنا بعّد بين أسفارنا [رَبُّنا بَعَّدَ]. Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Ḥasan, the brother of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, read فقالوا ربّنا بعد بين أسفارنا [رَبَّنا بَعُدَ بَيْنُ]. These are five readings. Al-Farrāʾ and Abū Isḥāq related the sixth: ربّنا بعد بين أسفارنا [رَبَّنا بَعُدَ بَيْنَ]. Abū Jaʿfar said: in the first reading ربّنا is accusative as a vocative in a construct (nidāʾ muḍāf); it is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because its meaning is "I called, I invoked". Likewise the second reading. «باعِد» and «بعِّد» are one in meaning, as you say قارِب and قرِّب. The meaning, according to what Muḥammad ibn Thawr related from Maʿmar from Qatāda, who said: they were secure; they would go out on their journeys without taking provisions, spending the night in one village and taking the midday rest in another; then they became insolent towards the blessing and said: "Our Lord, lengthen [the distance] between our journeys", so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, punished them.
In the third reading «ربُّنا» is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and «باعَدَ» is a past verb in the position of the khabar (predicate); likewise the fourth. Ibn ʿAbbās explained it; he said: they complained that their Lord had lengthened [the distance] between their journeys. The fifth reading is ربّنا بعُد بينُ أسفارنا: «ربّنا» is a vocative in a construct, then they made a statement after that, saying «بعُد بينُ أسفارنا» ("the span of our journeys has grown long"), with «بين» nominative by the verb, i.e. what connects to our journeys has grown long. The sixth reading is like this, except that it makes «بين» accusative as an adverb (ẓarf); its implied form in Arabic is "our travelling has grown long between our journeys". When these readings differ in their meanings, it may not be said that one of them is better than another — that is not said of reports when their meanings differ — rather, He reported of them that they prayed that [the distance] between their journeys be lengthened, out of insolence and arrogance, and He reported that when that was done to them they told of it and complained, as Ibn ʿAbbās said. ﴿وَظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾: i.e. by their disbelief. ﴿فَجَعَلْناهُمْ أَحادِيثَ﴾: i.e. their stories are told; its implied form in Arabic is "possessors of tales". ﴿وَمَزَّقْناهُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ﴾: i.e. when what befell them befell them, they dispersed and were torn apart. Al-Shaʿbī said:
So the Anṣār joined Yathrib, Ghassān Syria, Asad ʿUmān [Translator's note: so in the text; Azd is the usual name in this account], and Khuzāʿa Tihāma. ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ﴾: «صبّار» is the intensive of صابر. The ṣābir is the one who restrains himself from sins; he is praised with this name. If you mean that he persisted in sin, only صابر عن كذا ... is used for it. [Translator's note: this sentence is garbled in the printed text and is translated as written.] He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِنَّما يُوَفَّى الصَّابِرُونَ أَجْرَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ﴾ [al-Zumar: 10].

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
﴿وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِبْلِيسُ ظَنَّهُ﴾: there are four variant readings in it. [Translator's note: the vowelling of the variants has largely been lost in the printed text; the intended forms, reconstructed from the author's explanations, are given in square brackets.] Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read — and it is related from Mujāhid — ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَ﴾ with the light form, ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ إِبْلِيسُ﴾ with the nominative, ﴿ظَنَّهُ﴾ with the accusative. Ibn ʿAbbās, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read ﴿صَدَّقَ﴾ with the doubled form. Abū al-Hajhāj read ولقد صدق عليهم إبليسَ ظنُّه, with إبليس accusative and ظنّه nominative. Abū Ḥātim said: in my view this reading has no justification, and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best. Abū Jaʿfar said: al-Farrāʾ permitted this reading, and Abū Isḥāq mentioned it and said:
the meaning is: Iblīs's opinion proved Iblīs right, by their following him. The fourth reading is ولقد صدق عليهم إبليسُ ظنُّه, with both إبليس and ظنّه nominative. The first reading, ولقد صدَق عليهم إبليسُ ظنَّه, means "in his opinion"; Abū Isḥāq said: it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). The second reading, ولقد صدّق عليهم إبليسُ ظنَّه, has «ظنّه» accusative by the verb falling on it [as its object]. Mujāhid said: he held an opinion, and it turned out as he thought, so he confirmed his opinion. From Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Iblīs [said]: "Adam was created from clay, so he is weak, and I am from fire; I will surely bring his offspring under my sway, except a few"; and it was as he said. Al-Ḥasan said: he did not strike them with a whip or a stick; he only held an opinion, and it turned out as he thought, through his whispering. ﴿إِلَّا فَرِيقاً مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: accusative by the exception. There are two views on it: one is that some of the believers are meant by it; as for Ibn ʿAbbās, it is reported from him that he said: they are all the believers.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: [Translator's note: the entry concerns ﴿وَما كانَ لَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ سُلْطانٍ﴾.] ﴿مِنْ﴾ is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. The exegetes say: السلطان is the proof (al-ḥujja). ﴿إِلَّا لِنَعْلَمَ مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, already knew that as the unseen; this is the knowledge of what is witnessed, by which the proof becomes binding. This is the view of most of the philologists. According to some of them it is figurative, i.e. so that this be His knowledge on which He requites. A third view, which is the school of al-Farrāʾ, is that the meaning is "except that We may know that in your estimation", as He said ﴿أَيْنَ شُرَكائِيَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 27], i.e. according to your claim and in your estimation.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿قُلِ ادْعُوا الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾: there is an ellipsis in the passage; the meaning is: Say: call upon those whom you claimed to be gods for you besides Allah, that they may benefit you or ward off from you what Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has decreed against you; for they do not possess that. ﴿لا يَمْلِكُونَ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ فِي السَّماواتِ وَلا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَما لَهُمْ فِيهِما مِنْ شِرْكٍ وَما لَهُ مِنْهُمْ مِنْ ظَهِيرٍ﴾: al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Suddī said: i.e. of any helper.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
﴿أَذِنَ﴾ and أُذِنَ [Translator's note: the vowelling of the two forms is not shown in the printed text] are one in meaning, as has passed regarding وهل يُجازى [Sabaʾ: 17]. «مَن» here is for the intercessors, and it may be for those interceded for. Abū Isḥāq claimed that [its being] for the intercessors fits the meaning better; he said: because after it is ﴿حَتَّى إِذا فُزِّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾, so this would be for the angels, Allah's blessings be upon them. There are five readings in this. [Translator's note: the vowelling that distinguishes the readings has largely been lost in the printed text; the intended forms, reconstructed from the descriptions, are given in square brackets.] The reading of the generality is ﴿حَتَّى إِذا فُزِّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾; and from Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid: حتى إذا فَزَّع عن قلوبهم, with fatḥa on the fāʾ and the zāy. These two readings have one meaning, i.e. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, removed fear from their hearts, i.e. the fear passed beyond them. Sībawayh says likewise regarding the Arabs' saying رميت عن القوس, i.e. my shooting passed beyond the bow; and we have mentioned its meaning. Haytham [Translator's note: probably Hushaym is meant] related from ʿAwf from al-Ḥasan that he read حتى إذا فُرِّغ عن قلوبهم, with ḍamma on the fāʾ and with an undotted rāʾ followed by a dotted ghayn; and Abū Mijlaz read likewise. Maṭar al-Warrāq related from al-Ḥasan حتى إذا فزّع عن قلوبهم [فَرَّغ]. The meaning of these two readings comes back to the meaning of the first two, because the meaning is: until, when the fear was emptied from their hearts, [it was] removed from their hearts. However, Mujāhid said in explaining this verse, according to what Warqāʾ related from him via [Ibn] Abī Najīḥ:
it is on the Day of Resurrection. He said: when the covering is removed. Ayyūb and Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl related from al-Ḥasan حتى إذا فُرِغ عن قلوبهم, with ḍamma on the fāʾ, with a light (undoubled) undotted rāʾ followed by a dotted ghayn. These transmissions from al-Ḥasan have sound chains, with no flaw in any of those who related them, and all of them are authentic from him. ﴿قالُوا ماذا قالَ رَبُّكُمْ﴾: «ماذا» is in the position of the accusative by قال; and «ما» may be in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), with «ذا» in the position of the khabar (predicate), its meaning being that of الذي ("that which"). ﴿قالُوا الْحَقَّ﴾: on the basis that «ماذا» is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "He said the truth"; and the nominative of «الحقّ» is permissible on the basis that ما is in the position of the nominative. ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and khabar. «العليّ» is the Compeller, the Exalted; and «الكبير» is the Lord to whom one turns.
